newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends mostly up but off session highs.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends mostly up but off session highs.

text.p: WCE canola futures settled higher but sharply off session highs in a bout of late-session commercial selling and farmer hedging, traders said.
The canola trading session reflected the CBOT soybean prices, which rose early and then sold off at the close.

"Chicago dropped like a rock and we came down with them," a trader said. CBOT soybeans closed 2-3/4 to six cents per bushel lower amid talk the weather outlook in Brazil was turning more favorable for crops.

But flax seed maintained its gains with light farmer hedging and good commercial scale-down buying from the highs, he said. January canola was up $1.60 at $403.00 a tonne and January flax jumped $3.30 to $350.00.
February western barley gained $1.30 to $135.70 and March feed wheat edged up $0.90 to $168.80.

One analyst cited several factors which included light hedge selling, no deliveries, commercial buying and short covering. There were also expectations the Canadian Wheat Board will be aggressive in the barley tenders involving Saudi Arabia and potentially Iran, he said.
Saudi Arabia will tender on Tuesday for 1.2 million tonnes of barley from optional origins, European traders have said.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
